title: operational-telemetry-hypotheses-and-visualization-guide
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact set of operational hypotheses, metric definitions, trace anchors, and dashboard layout ideas intended to reduce investigation time for perceived latency regressions and cache-cold episodes. It surfaces a new pattern we99re calling the "latency thermostat": automated sampling and probe intensity that scales with SLO pressure to keep trace budget predictable without losing fidelity when incidents matter.

Context and motivation:
- Observability load is growing (more models, multi-tenant routing, varied sequence lengths). We cannot afford full sampling at all times.
- Operators need quick heuristics to decide whether an incident is a routing/capacity issue, model-level stall, or client pattern (large context, long generation).
- Current dashboards scatter signals across many panels; investigators spend 10-30m stitching session traces, KV cache state, and model variant metadata.

High-level hypotheses (to be validated):
1) Most high-p99 perceived-latency incidents correlate with either a) prefix cache misses on hot-tenants or b) backend routing to cheaper (higher-latency) model variants.
2) Targeted increase in trace sampling (thermostat) when SLO heating occurs yields high signal gain with limited trace-cost increase.
3) A compact 3-tier dashboard (heatmap slice, session replay list, span waterfall) reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR) by >30%.

Metric and signal definitions (canonical names and descriptions):
- request.latency_ms.p50/p95/p99: end-to-end request latency measured at API gateway ingress to response flush. Unit: ms.
- token.gen.latency_ms.p50/p95/p99: per-token generation latency measured inside serving runtime (includes kernel time + queue wait). Unit: ms.
- kv.prefix.hit_rate: ratio of requests served from prefix/KV cache vs total that needed prefix. Range 0-1.
- kv.eviction_rate_per_min: count of eviction ops per minute per host. Unit: evictions/min.
- routing.fallback_rate: fraction of requests that were routed to fallback model variant due to capacity or health.
- model.variant.swap_count: number of model instance swaps (reloads/rollouts) per host per hour.
- tenant.cold_cache_fraction: fraction of sessions for a tenant where KV cache warmedness < 0.2 at request start.
- session.length.tokens: context+response tokens per session; useful for slicing latency.
- sdp.queue_time_ms: scheduler dispatch queue time before model invocation.

Suggested derived metrics (aggregation rules):
- perceived_latency.p99_by_tenant: p99 request.latency_ms grouped by tenant, last 15m sliding.
- kv_warmth_index: weighted combination of tenant.cold_cache_fraction and kv.prefix.hit_rate to rank tenants needing priming probes.
- trace_budget_utilization: fraction of daily trace-sample budget consumed; integrates thermostat controller input.

Tracing surface and span design (minimal semantic spec):
Span name conventions (keep short, deterministic):
- span:api.request (attributes: request_id, tenant_id, route, model_requested)
- span:router.decision (attributes: candidate_model, chosen_model, reason_code, fallback)
- span:queue.wait (attributes: queue_name, position, estimated_wait_ms)
- span:runtime.invoke (attributes: host_id, container_id, model_hash, quantization, kernel_selector)
- span:runtime.kv_lookup (attributes: prefix_key, hit=true|false, kv_latency_ms, eviction_flag)
- span:model.step (attributes: step_index, tokens_generated, batch_size)
- span:response.stream (attributes: bytes_sent, final=true|false)
Important span attributes (for indexing/filtering):
- tenant_id, request_id, model_hash, host_bucket (zone/region), kv_hit, fallback=true|false, sequence_length, prompt_variant_id

Adaptive sampling rules (latency thermostat concept):
- Normal mode: probabilistic sampling at 0.2% of requests, bias towards high-cost tenants and long sessions (session.length.tokens > 2048).
- Heating mode (SLO breach window): when perceived_latency.p95 > SLO_threshold for 5m, increase sampling to 5% for requests that meet either (tenant in top 10 by request volume) OR (kv.prefix.hit_rate < 0.6).
- Critical mode: when perceived_latency.p99 exceeds SLO_threshold by 2x or error rate spikes, temporarily enable 20% sampling for 10 minutes focused on requests with fallback=true OR queue_time_ms > 50ms.
- Cooling: when p95 returns below threshold for 10m, stair-step down sampling (5% -> 1% -> 0.2%) to avoid oscillation.
- Budget guard: global trace_budget_utilization cannot exceed 80% of daily budget; if reached, fall back to top-k tenant sampling and synthetic probes.

Dashboard composition (three-panel compact layout):
1) Thermostat heatmap (left): 3D-lookup grid: tenants (rows) x latency buckets (cols) x kv_warmth_index (color). Interaction: click tenant -> middle panel.
2) Investigation list (center): Top 40 session snippets over last 15m for selected tenant slice. Columns: timestamp, request_id, model_hash, request.latency_ms, kv_hit, route_decision. Quick actions: open trace, attach eval prompt. Sortable and searchable.
3) Span waterfall + timeline (right): waterfall of selected session trace with annotated span anchors (router.decision, runtime.kv_lookup, runtime.invoke). Inline notes for operators: common signatures -> recommended next step (e.g., "kv miss -> prime tenant cache with synthetic probe").
Additional widgets (below):
- SLO summary strip: p50/p95/p99 + error rate by region and by model variant.
- Probe panel: synthetic probe pass/fail and last warm status per tenant.
- Cost meter: token emission rate and estimated inference cost per minute to help tradeoff debugging vs cost.

Investigation playbook (compact steps):
1) Surface: check SLO summary + thermostat heatmap -> identify tenant or region hot cell.
2) Correlate: open investigation list -> filter for requests with kv_hit=false and high queue_time_ms.
3) Trace drill: open waterfall for 2-3 outlier sessions. Look for long runtime.invoke spans or router.decision fallback reasons.
4) Action: if kv misses dominate, run tenant primer (synthetic warm probes), schedule tenant-level prewarm cron, or raise tenant weight to pin model in cache. If fallback evident, investigate capacity pools and autoscaler logs.
5) Post-mortem: annotate first bad trace with root cause tag and link to team/PR.

Instrumentation checklist (developer handoff):
- [ ] Ensure all request entry/exit points set request_id and tenant_id.
- [ ] Add kv.lookup span with kv_hit boolean and key namespace.
- [ ] Add router.decision span with chosen_model and reason_code.
- [ ] Emit queue_time_ms metric at scheduler boundaries.
- [ ] Tag model_hash and quantization params on runtime.invoke spans.
- [ ] Emit session.length.tokens at session close.

Search/query snippets (examples for dashboards and alerts):
- High-p99 tenants (last 15m):
  SELECT tenant_id, PERCENTILE_CONT(latency_ms, 0.99) as p99 FROM requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '15m' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY p99 DESC LIMIT 50;

- Top kv miss sessions:
  SELECT request_id, tenant_id, latency_ms, kv_hit FROM requests WHERE kv_hit = false AND ts > now() - interval '30m' ORDER BY latency_ms DESC LIMIT 100;

- Trace-driven alert condition (thermostat trigger):
  ALERT if perceived_latency.p95 > SLO and trace_budget_utilization < 0.8 -> set sampling_state = HEATING for implicated tenants.

Operational concerns and open questions:
- How to reliably map model_hash -> human-friendly model name in dashboards (need small metadata service or periodic sync).
- Interaction with tenant-level rate limiting: if we increase sampling, will we hit tenant quotas? Need guard rails.
- Synthetic probe design: what amplitude/frequency primes cache without causing load spikes? Default suggestion: 3x small probes/minute for top 20 tenants when kv_warmth_index < 0.3.
- Compliance: trace payloads may contain PII in prompts. Need automatic redaction pipeline for spans and attributes before longer retention.

Next steps (short roadmap):
- Nov 2025: prototype thermostat controller (feature toggle + metric hooks) and add simple heatmap widget. Owner: Priya.
- Dec 2025: implement span naming standard and update runtime instrumentation. Owner: Evan.
- Jan 2026: pilot increased sampling on two high-volume tenants; measure trace budget impact and MTTR. Owner: Maya.
- Feb 2026: iterate dashboard UX based on pilot feedback; add probe priming automation. Owner: Diego.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight; please call out missing signals you rely on regularly during investigations.
- If you have a different name preference for the "thermostat" pattern, suggest alternatives (controller, probe governor, sampling governor).

Changelog:
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-11-21: added sampling stair-step and budget guard (Evan)
- 2026-03-08: updated dashboard wireframe and query snippets, expanded instrumentation checklist (Maya)

End of doc.
